title: Effect of a head-only move
statement: Let $c,C,q$ be natural numbers, let $x$ and $o$ be finite Boolean words, let $s,s'$ be control states for parameters $c,C$, let $h$ assign an integer position to each of the $c+1$ work tapes, and choose a work-tape index $i$ and a direction $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$. Applying the action that moves only head $i$ by $d$ and enters state $s'$ to the configuration with input $x$, state $s$, unary tape contents of length $q$, head positions $h$, and output $o$ gives the configuration with the same input, tape contents, and output, state $s'$, and head positions equal to $h$ except that position $i$ is $h(i)+d$.
hypotheses_covered: $h$ assigns an integer position to each of the $c+1$ work tapes
replaced:
For every work-tape index $i$ and direction $d$, applying the head-only move
action for $i$, $d$, and a target state to a generator loop configuration
yields the loop configuration in that target state whose $i$-th work-head
position is increased by $d$; all tapes, the input position, the other
heads, and the output are unchanged.
